Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful one: the ability to automatically change your passwords for you.

iOS 27's Passwords app, powered by Apple Intelligence, can fix compromised credentials on your behalf

The next generation of Apple Intelligence will be central to the upcoming iOS 27 and its accompanying software updates, including a powerful new AI feature for the Apple Passwords app.

The Passwords app launched two years ago as a dedicated hub for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always told you when passwords in your database are problematic. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will alert you.

But until now, you've always had to manually fix those problematic credentials yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says its new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to their website:

With this feature, you can always keep your credentials secure and use strong enough passwords without spending much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to launch officially for all users in the coming weeks. This new Passwords feature is expected to ship with iOS 27.0, though its availability in beta has been spotty, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has your experience been? Share with us in the comments.
